assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses turned transmission electron microscopy into a routine sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom probe of interfaces, defects, oxides and nanostructures. It is a clear, original instrument invention with large lasting impact across physics, materials science and chemistry, which fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion. I note that this is close to my own field, so I have tried to judge it by the same standard I would apply elsewhere.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider led the realization of the hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban led the demonstration for the high-resolution and materials applications. These three names are a natural and fairly clean configuration. Other groups, notably the Krivanek line of work in STEM correction, are not in the supplied credit, so the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Aberration-corrected instruments have been widely deployed for about two decades and are independently reproduced in many laboratories. The method is mature and the recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied three-name credit adequately covers the TEM and STEM correction lines is unresolved; I have not independently verified priority details.
The prize could be seen as honoring an enabling instrument rather than a single physical discovery, though the invention route is explicit in the criteria.
My professional proximity to the field may bias my judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuinely new type of semiconductor laser based on engineered intersubband transitions in heterostructures, not on bandgap emission. It opened mid-infrared and terahertz sources used in spectroscopy and sensing. It is an original invention with clear lasting impact and demonstrates quantum engineering of electronic states.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 demonstration at Bell Labs was by Faist, Capasso and collaborators, with Cho's molecular-beam epitaxy crucial for the layer quality. Capasso, Faist and Cho form a plausible trio, though other Bell Labs co-authors and earlier proposals (e.g. Kazarinov and Suris, 1971) complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of continuous development, commercial adoption and independent replication make this fully mature. If anything, it is overdue.
uncertainties: Priority questions regarding the early intersubband proposal and the role of other Bell Labs co-authors remain.
Some may judge the work as device engineering rather than discovery; I regard it as a physical invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength trapping idea with many-atom interrogation to reach fractional uncertainties near the 10^-18 level. It has redefined precision timekeeping, enables tests of fundamental constants and relativistic redshift at the centimetre scale, and is a clear invention with lasting consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early realizations, and Ye's group pushed it to record accuracy and many-body interrogation. A two-person configuration is clean. It is possible that others, such as ion-clock and optical-frequency-comb pioneers, are seen as having been recognized already (Hall and Hänsch received the 2005 prize), which supports separate recognition here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and advanced optical lattice clocks, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. This is mature and timely.
uncertainties: I have not independently verified all priority details of the early proposals.
The relation to the earlier comb and ion-clock recognition might raise questions about overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells launched topological insulators as a new class of matter, linking band topology to robust edge transport. It is highly original, and its lasting impact on condensed-matter physics is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the founding prediction, and Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive experiment. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realization, and other groups also contributed to the three-dimensional case, so the credit is not simple. The supplied list is a defensible configuration, but contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and widely reproduced, including in three-dimensional materials; the interpretation is stable. Timely and arguably somewhat overdue, although the 2016 prize already recognized topological phases of matter.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction and the 3D extension is not covered by the supplied names.
The partial overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases must be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices give tunable realizations of Hubbard-type models and made quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter experimentally real. The observation of the superfluid-to-Mott transition, together with the theoretical proposal, defined a field. Impact is broad.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) provided the theoretical proposal, Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott transition, and Esslinger's group showed fermionic Mott insulators and related control. Limiting to three names forces a hard choice; the list contains four, and Jaksch is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and very active. Recognition is timely, though the field is still maturing in terms of practical quantum advantage.
uncertainties: Selecting three of four names is difficult, and Esslinger's role could be argued to be equally decisive.
Overlap with the 2012 and 2001 prizes on quantum control and condensates should be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting phases in twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré quantum matter, a very active area with real novelty and strong interdisciplinary impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. A theory-plus-experiment split is natural, but there are other contributors such as Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto who are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The effect is reproduced widely, but the interpretation of the correlated phases and superconductivity is still under debate, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Prior theoretical contributions not in the credited names could change the allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-quality hexagonal boron nitride crystals and their use as substrates and encapsulation made van der Waals heterostructures with high mobility possible, enabling fractional quantum Hall and moiré physics in graphene. It is an enabling materials advance of large impact, with the discovery character being less direct than for a new phenomenon. As a materials physicist I value the importance of crystal quality, but I weigh the discovery criterion carefully.
assessment.attribution: Watanabe and Taniguchi grew the crystals, and Dean demonstrated the graphene-on-hBN devices. Credit as an enabling contribution is distributed across many device groups, so this is a pragmatic but contestable trio.
assessment.maturity: Universally used in the field and independently confirmed for over a decade. Mature, although the recognition may be seen as supportive infrastructure for other discoveries.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the committee would treat crystal growth as a stand-alone discovery or invention.
The role of Dean versus other device pioneers is ambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides, followed rapidly by transition temperatures above 50 K, opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors beyond cuprates. This is a clear discovery with independent confirmation, though a mechanism remains unresolved.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group reported the original LaFeAsO(F) result, and the Chen and Zhao groups quickly raised the transition temperature in related compounds. Hosono is clearly central, while the credit of the other two is more derivative and the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories, but the pairing mechanism is not understood and practical applications are limited. Recognition could be viewed as either timely or leaning on the unresolved physics.
uncertainties: Whether Chen and Zhao should share credit with Hosono is a genuine question.
